title: Gluing the local trace discriminant ideals
statement: For a finite flat morphism $f:X \to Y$ of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with $Y$ locally Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], there exists a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $J$ on $Y$ such that every $y \in Y$ has an affine neighbourhood $U$, an integer $n \geq 0$, and a basis $b$ indexed by $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ for $\Gamma(f^{-1}U,\mathcal O_X)$ over $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Y)$, for the algebra structure induced by $f$, with $J(U)=(d_b)$. Here $d_b$ is the determinant of the matrix with entries $\operatorname{Tr}(m_{b_i b_j})$, where $m_a$ is multiplication by $a$.

source.place: Tag 0BVH, construction of the discriminant before discriminant-lemma-discriminant

proof.text: On an affine target chart the finite source is affine. Its section algebra is a finite flat module over the Noetherian section ring, hence finitely presented and locally free. Refine the target chart to principal affine opens where this module has a finite basis. On each such chart take the principal ideal generated by the determinant of the trace matrix in that basis. Trace of endomorphisms of finite free modules commutes with localization. If the basis is changed by an invertible matrix P, the trace matrix changes by congruence, so its determinant is multiplied by det(P)^2, a unit. Thus these principal ideals agree on overlaps, after a common affine refinement, and glue to a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf J. Each point is contained in one of the chosen charts; its basis and the formula for J are the witnesses below. The rank can vary from chart to chart. For rank zero the determinant of the empty matrix is one, giving the unit ideal. No regularity or nonvanishing of the determinant is needed.

theorem exists_ideal_locally_eq_trace_discriminant_of_finite_flat
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f] [Flat f] :
    ∃ J : Y.IdealSheafData, ∀ y : Y, ∃ U : Y.affineOpens, y ∈ U.1 ∧
      (letI := (f.app U.1).hom.toAlgebra
       ∃ (n : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) Γ(Y, U.1) Γ(X, f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)),
         J.ideal U = Ideal.span {Algebra.discr Γ(Y, U.1) b})
